goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
goldens.reasoning: C1 points out the same problem: negative slicing on a Django queryset.

goldens.comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
goldens.reasoning: None of the candidates mention the AttributeError when member is None.

goldens.comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
goldens.reasoning: C2 points out the same problem: math.floor/ceil called on a datetime.
None of the candidates mention the import of a class that doesn't exist.

candidates: Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing - when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, line 882 passes the negative offset directly to queryset[start_offset:stop], which raises AssertionError. Any superuser hitting the audit logs endpoint with optimized_pagination=true and a crafted cursor containing a negative offset will get a 500 error. The fix should clamp start_offset to 0 or reject negative offsets with a BadPaginationError.

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor()/math.ceil() directly on datetime objects (line 839), which raises TypeError since datetime does not implement __floor__. The method should convert datetime to float timestamp first like DateTimePaginator does.

OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value (an integer timestamp) instead of converting it back to a datetime, so build_queryset will compare an integer against a DateTimeField on page 2+, causing type mismatch errors. It should convert back using datetime.fromtimestamp() like DateTimePaginator does.
